tickle in Latin

tickle

tītillō, tītillāre · tītillātiō, tītillātiōnis f.

Ancient LatinQuotationsComposed phrasesDraft
  • tītillō, tītillāre — tickle classical (Lucr. 2.429; Cic. Fin. 1.39) Classical writers mostly use the verb of pleasure tickling the senses.
  • tītillātiō, tītillātiōnis f. — tickling classical (Cic. N.D. 1.113; Cic. Sen. 47; Sen. Ep. 92.6)
  • tītillātus, tītillātūs m. — tickling classical also used (Plin. NH 11.198)
  • praecipua hilaritātis sēdēs, quod tītillātū maximē intellegitur ālārum — [the diaphragm is] the chief seat of laughter, as tickling the armpits shows best (Plin. NH 11.198)
  • Tītillābō tē! — I’m going to tickle you! composed
  • Ubi tītillem? Sub ālīs? — Where shall I tickle you? Under your arms? composed
  • Nōlī mē tītillāre! — Don’t tickle me! composed

See also: hiccup.
